Elena — thanks, answered inline below and included an example calculation. Short answers first:
1) We propose a fixed dollar cap for the window (easier for AP). Example: a $25k not-to-exceed for the 14-day launch window.
2) Usage is measured server-side per UTC day by token, consistent with your existing metering. We’ll provide the raw per-day token export with the true-up.
3) This would be an amendment (DocuSign) to your current contract but scoped only to the two-week window (no permanent change to your quota).

Example (using your peak estimate of 1.2M tokens/day):
- Expected baseline (committed quota): 30M tokens for the month = ~1M/day average
- Peak days (estimated): 10 days at 1.2M/day = +2M tokens above baseline over the 14-day window
- Normal overrun rate: $0.00035/token -> overrun cost = 2,000,000 * $0.00035 = $700
- Capped overrun proposal: limit additional spend to $3,500 for the window (blended overrun cap; example blended rate would be ~ $0.0003/token until cap hit)

We intentionally set the cap conservatively; if Acumen prefers a stricter firm cap we can move to $2,000 and adjust the blended per-token rate.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm AP is okay with a single fixed-dollar cap for the window (this simplifies reconciliation).
- If yes, I’ll generate DocuSign amendment and attach the token export template and MAP for sign-off.

Elena — quick add from finance side. Two practical variants we've used with other customers:

A) Fixed-cap true-up (Naomi's suggestion): single invoice for any overrun up to the not-to-exceed cap. AP-friendly.
B) Pro-rated temporary rate lift: temporarily increase committed capacity price for the launch window (e.g., a 10% uplift on committed units for 14 days) and apply normal metered billing; this avoid a separate overrun invoice but requires a simple PO amendment.

If AP wants minimal paperwork, option A is lowest friction. If they want to avoid an "overrun" line item on the invoice, option B looks cleaner in the finance system. Both can be implemented as short DocuSign amendments; they only differ in how we represent the charge.

Also attaching a sample true-up invoice layout (see redwood-temp-uplift-pricing-v2.pdf) so AP can see what the single invoice would look like.
